data.long_meaning: The name Beaver comes from the English word for the animal, which is known for its hardworking and industrious nature. Beavers are known for building dams and lodges, and their name symbolizes diligence and determination. The name Beaver carries the meaning “Hardworking, industrious” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English. Parents who choose Beaver usually hope their child will grow to embody hardworking, industrious and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Beaver has been used as a given name since the Middle Ages, and was popular in Europe during the 14th and 15th centuries. In North America, Beaver was a common surname among the French and English settlers. The name gained additional popularity in the 19th century when the fur trade became an important industry, and beaver pelts were highly valued for their fur. Today, the name Beaver is mostly found in English-speaking countries, and is often associated with hard work and determination.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Beaver can be seen as a reminder of the importance of hard work and perseverance. The beaver's ability to build dams and lodges is an impressive feat, and can be seen as a symbol of the human capacity to create and build. Additionally, the name Beaver can be seen as a reflection of the Biblical concept of stewardship, as beavers use the resources of their environment to build their homes. Ultimately, the name Beaver encourages us to be diligent and resourceful in our own lives, and to use the gifts and resources around us to build something meaningful and lasting.
